plain_description.what: On 597 quantitative questions (math, physics, chemistry, engineering), the reference model wrote a Python program that was executed in a sandbox, and its answer was compared with the usual cached reasoning reference.
plain_description.why: It tests whether a stronger kind of reference (computed, not reasoned) would help the judge in quantitative cells.
plain_description.information: More correct answers would justify a per-cell reference form and a judged follow-up. No gain closes the idea. Result: done; the judged stage was never run. The program-based reference was right on exactly as many questions as the usual one (464 of 482). The two agreed 98% of the time and often repeated the same mistakes, so the remaining errors are modelling errors, not arithmetic slips. The idea is closed for this corpus. Older question family, later ruled 'history, not evidence'.
